......
 JUDGMENT The Petitioner has filed this petition under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road accident dated 19.09.2017.

2. The case of the Petitioner in brief is that, on 19.09.2017 at about 6.00 p.m., the petitioner was a crossing the road on the extreme left side on PavagadaTumkur road, in front of Yamaha Show room, Banashankari, Pavagada Town, Tumkur, at that time suddenly the rider of TVS Apchi bike bearing Engine No.BRICH2004673 (Engine and Chassis No.H2004673C04187) came from SSK Samudaya Bhavana towards MAG circle in a rash and negligent manner endangering to human life,
without observing any of the Traffic rules and regulations and dashed against him and caused the accident, as a result he fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body, immediately he was shifted to near Srikanth Hospital, Pavagada, wherein first aid treatment was given and for further management referred to M.S.Ramaiah Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein admitted as an inpatient from 20.09.2017 to 29.09.2017 and underwent surgery i.e., CRIF with IMIL Nail left 10 x 38 tibia nail, right 10x38 tibia nail (sharma) on 21.09.2017 and discharged with an advise and he is still continuing follow up treatments.

So far spent more than Rs.2,00,000/ towards medical,
conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges etc., and the doctor have also advised him to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants in near future, incurring huge expenses.

3. The petitioner further submitted that, at the time of accident he was hale and healthy and was running provision stores, apart from doing agriculture work and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/ per month.

Due to the accidental injuries he not attended to his work, resulted in loss of earning,
earning capacity and put to great financial hardship.
He is suffering from permanent disability and deformity.

The Pavagad Police have registered a criminal case and filed charge sheet against the rider of the TVS Apchi bike bearing Engine No.BRICH2004673 (Engine and Chassis No.H2004673C04187) in Cr.No.220/2017 u/Sec.279, 338 of IPC.
The 1st respondent being the owner and the 2nd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to him.
4. In response to service of notice issued by this court/Tribunal, the Respondent No.2 has appeared and filed written statement.
In spite of due service of summons, the Respondent No.1 did not appear and hence placed exparte.

5. The Respondent No.2 in the written statement have denied the case of the petitioner as false,
admitted issuance of policy but subject to terms and conditions and submitted that there is non compliance of Section 134(c) and Section 158(6) of M.V. Act.

Further submitted the jurisdictional police after investigation filed the chargesheet against the 1st respondent, the accused rider/owner Sri.Ramappa vs Mr.Narendra on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187077521/
2 of Sec.279 & 338 of IPC, under Section 134 (A&B) 187 & 181 of MV Act.

The 1st respondent/owner of the vehicle, willfully and by knowingly ridden the vehicle without having the valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident and hence there is breach of policy conditions.

Therefore,
prayed for dismissal of the petition against him.
6. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues were framed:

1 . Whether the Petitioner proves that on 19.09.2017 at about 6.00 p.m., while he was proceeding as a pedestrian, infront of Yamaha Showroom, Banashankari, Pavagada Tumkur road, Pavagada town, Tumkur, the rider of TVS Apachi bike bearing Engine No.BRICH2004673 (Engine and Chassis No.H2004673C04187), driven the same in a high speed, rash and negligent manner and dashed against him and caused accident, resulting which he sustained injuries?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for Compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3.
What order or award?
7. The Petitioner in order to prove his case, he has examined himself as PW.1 and got marked documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.21.

Sri.Raviprakash Hospital attendant in MRD Department at M.S.Ramaiah Hospital, Bangalore, is examined as PW.2 and produced documents as per Exs.P22 to P.25 and also examined Dr.Nagaraj B.N. Orthopedic Surgeon at Sai Ortho And Dental Center, as PW.3 and produced documents as per Exs.P26 and P27.

On the other side the Respondent No.2 has examined its official as RW.1 and produced documents as per Exs.R1 to R4.
8.
Heard the arguments and perused the materials on record.
The counsel for the petitioner filed written arguments on his behalf.

The counsel for the respondent no.2 has relied upon decisions as follows; 1)AIR 2020 SC 4453: Beli Ram Vs. Rajinder Kumar & Anr., 2) 2019 ACJ 409: Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd., Vs. Annemma & Ors.,
9.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On hearing both sides and perusal of the evidence on record this court answers the above issues as follows: Issue No.1: In the affirmative, Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative, Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following: REASONS 10. Issue No.1: The Petitioner in order to prove that the accident was occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the TVS Apachi bike bearing Engine No.BRICH2004673 (Engine and Chassis No.H2004673 C04187) has examined himself as PW.1 and produced 11 documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.4, P7 to P13.

He has specifically stated in his evidence that, on 19.09.2017 at about 6.00 p.m., he was crossing the road on the extreme left side on PavagadaTumkur road, in front of Yamaha Show room, Banashankari, Pavagada Town, Tumkur, at that time suddenly the rider of TVS Apchi bike bearing Engine No.BRICH2004673 (Engine and Chassis No.H2004673 C04187) came from SSK Samudaya Bhavana towards MAG circle in a rash and negligent manner endangering to human life, without observing any of the Traffic rules and Sri.Ramappa vs Mr.Narendra on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187077521/
3 regulations and dashed against him and caused the accident.

The Respondent No.2 insurer has denied the case of the petitioner as false and contended that there was breach of policy conditions and hence if any compensation is awarded they are not liable to indemnify the insured.
In the cross examination of PW.1 nothing worth is elicited to disprove the alleged manner of accident.

11. Though the respondent no.2 has examined its official as RW.1 but his evidence is more focused on their defence that the rider of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective DL as on the date of accident and hence not helpful to prove their defence that there was negligence on the part of the petitioner.

12. Further, the Petitioner apart from his oral evidence has produced the documents such as FIR,
FIS, chargesheet, police notice, spot mahazar, IMV report, certified copy of Indemnity Bond,
certified copy of Indemnity bond dated 27.10.2017, statement of witnesses, certified copy of ordersheet in CC No.284/2018, and notice issued by I.O. to Medical officer as per Exs.P.1 to P.4, P7 to P13 and they are public documents which have got presumptive value under law and in absence of contrary evidence the said documents needs to be appreciated in favour of petitioner.

The Ex.P.3 which is the copy of charge sheet filed in Cr.No.220/2017 clearly discloses that the investigation officer has filed chargesheet after detail investigation holding that the rider of the offending vehicle had ridden it in a rash and negligent manner with high speed and caused the accident.
The contents of documents produced by the Petitioner as per Exs.P.1 to P.4, P7 to P13 are fully and completely corroborated with oral evidence of the Petitioner.
As such, there are no reasons to disbelieve the version of the Petitioner and accept the version of the Respondent No.2.
Further the wound certificate produced that Ex.P5 clear shows that the account of accident the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with the documents produced as per Exs.P.1 to P.4, P7 to P13, this court is of the opinion that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the TVS Apachi Bike bearing Engine No.BRICH2004673 (Engine & Chassis No.H2004673C04187) and same has resulted in grievous injuries to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, issue No.1 is held in the affirmative.

13. Issue No.2: The Petitioner has further averred that, on account of accident, he was completely bed ridden, getting head ache and giddiness often, cannot walk, stand, cannot use Indian type toilet,
cannot lift or carry weight, due to severe facial injuries, there are scar marks present over the face which is looking ugly and undergoing deep mental shock, pain sustained and it has caused him permanent disability and hence he is unable to do his earlier work/occupation.
The Petitioner in this regard has entered into witness box and deposed that due to the accidental injuries, he is suffering from permanent disability.
Apart from that, he has produced the wound certificate as per Ex.P.5.

As per Ex.P.5, the Petitioner has sustained injury to both right leg and left leg with multiple abrasions over the body, xray of right leg shows tibial shaft fracture proximal third and fibula bone fracture and 2nd xray of left leg shows tibial shaft fracture middle third and fibula fracture, the doctor opined that injuries are grievous in nature.
The petitioner got examined Dr.Raviprakash B.G. as PW.2 and also examined Dr.Nagaraj H.N. as PW.3.
This court while considering the Issue No.1 has already come to the conclusion that the accident occurred due to the rash or negligent riding of the rider of TVS Appachi motorcycle.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation from the Respondents.

Sri.Ramappa vs Mr.Narendra on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187077521/

14.

sentences.text: The PW.2Mr

. Raviprakash B.G. Hospital attendant in MRD Department at M.S.Ramaiah Hospital, has produced documents as Exs.P22 to P25 which are authorization letter, true copy of MLC register extract, one inpatient casesheet and one outpatient casesheet.
From his evidence and the documents it can be make out that the petitioner took treatment in the said hospital.

In the cross examination of PW.2 nothing worth is elicited and the respondent no.2 has not lead any contrary evidence to disprove the documents produced by the PW.2.
15.

In the chiefexamination, the PW.3 has deposed that, a patient by name Mr.Ramappa, aged about 74 years came to him on 16.02.2023 for assessment of disability and he gave an alleged H/o RTA on 19.09.2017, did sustain left tibia middle third fracture and right tibia fracture and as per the copy of the discharge summary, he was treated at M.S.Ramaiah Hospital, with CRIF with IMIL nail for both tibia on 21.09.2017 and later discharged with an advise and the fractures united and he now complains of weakness and pain in both lower limb, unable to lift weights, unable to sit down, squat and sit cross leg and he has healed scar over both the knees, restricted both knee movements,
wasting of the both thigh muscles and recent xray of the both the legs shows united fracture tibia fracture with implant insitu.

PW.3 further deposed that he examined the petitioner clinically,
radiologically for assessment of disability and petitioner has got permanent physical disability of the right lower limb is at 38%, left lower limb is at 43% and to the whole body 25% which is permanent in nature and the petitioner needs another surgery for removal of implant which costs Rs.60,000/.
In the crossexamination of PW.3 it is brought out that he has not treated the petitioner, he has not seen old xray, casesheet and other medical record of the petitioner.
Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, the period of treatment that he has undergone, his age, his functional disability is considered at 14% to the whole body.
Monthly income.

16. The Petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, he was running provision stores apart from doing agricultural work and earning sum of Rs.30,000/ per month and due to accident he could not attend to his work.

Further, to substantiate the income the Petitioner has not produced any relevant document to prove that he was getting income from provision store and agricultural work such as the bank statement, agriculture produce sale bills or receipts etc., to ascertain his income or examined any witness in this regard.
Therefore, the version of the Petitioner that he was earning a sum of Rs.30,000/ per month is not acceptable.
At the time of accident the Petitioner was aged about 68 years as could be make out from Ex.P15/Adhaar card of the petitioner is shows that his date of birth is 01.01.1949.
The accident took place in the year 2017.

In absence of specific evidence for income, therefore, by taking judicial notice of hike in the cost of living and also relying the decision of Hon'ble H.C. in the case of Sumangala & Others and Ramanagouda &Anr., in MFA No:202534/2019(MVC) wherein the notified notional income chart of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority is considered for fixing the notional income and accordingly the monthly notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.11,000/ per month.

As such, Petitioner is entitled for the following compensation:
Sri.Ramappa vs Mr.Narendra on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187077521/
5 i) PAIN AND SUFFERING:

After the accident, the Petitioner was taken to Srikanth Hospital,
Pavagada, wherein first at treatment was taken and then shifted to M.S.Ramaiah Hospital,
Bengaluru, treated as an inpatient from 20.09.2017 to 29.09.2017 for 10 days as per Ex.P.6/Discharge summary and underwent surgery CRIF with IMIL Nail left 10x38, tibia nail, right 10x38 tibia nail (sharma).
Therefore, considering the nature of injuries and duration of treatment he has underwent, the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.55,000/ under this head.
ii) LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:
As mentioned above the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries
After the accident, the Petitioner was taken treatment in the above mentioned hospitals.
Therefore, considering the nature of injuries and the duration of treatment it can be said that the Petitioner has required at least two months time for recovering from the injuries sustained by him.
Hence, he is entitled for a sum of Rs.22,000/ under this head.
iii) MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The petitioner claimed that he incurred Rs.2,00,000/ towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges etc.,
In this regard, he has produced 68 medical bills for Rs.1,33,558/ as per Ex.P.14.
In the cross examination of PW.1 nothing worth is elicited to disprove the said bills and moreover the respondent no.2 has not lead any contrary evidence to these bills.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.1,33,558/ under the heads of Medical Expenses.
iv) LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME:
In so far as age of the Petitioner is concerned, the Aadhaar card is produced as per Ex.P.15.
As per this document his age was 68 years as on the date of accident.
Therefore, as on the date of the accident the Petitioner's age is considered as 68 years.
As per Sarala Verma's case the appropriate multiplier applicable to his age is 5.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled a sum of Rs.92.400/ (Rs.11,000/ x 12 x 5 x14%= Rs.92,400/) under this head.
(v) LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND  HAPPINESS:
The Petitioner was aged about 68 years at the time of accident.
He has sustained grievous injuries and as per consideration of this Tribunal, he is suffering from 14% permanent disability.
The Petitioner has to suffer this disability throughout his life.
Because of this he will have to lose some amenities and comforts.
Therefore, considering the age and nature of injuries that the Petitioner has suffered a sum of Rs.17,000/ is awarded under this head.
vi) ATTENDANT, CONVEYANCE, FOOD AND  NOURISHMENT CHARGES:
After the accident, the Petitioner took treatment in two hospitals.
He was treated as an inpatient at M.S.Ramaiah Hospital for 10 days and underwent surgery.
Therefore, as during this period he must have spent considerable amount on his conveyance, attendant charges, food and nourishment etc..
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.17,000/ under this head.
Sri.Ramappa vs Mr.Narendra on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187077521/
6 (vii) FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:
As per the version of the PW.3, he needs another surgery for the removal of the implant the estimate of this surgery is around Rs.60,000/.
But there is no estimation bill produced by the Petitioner or PW.3.
Looking to the earlier treatment cost and nature of injury and evidence on record, it appears it would be justifiable if an amount of Rs.20,000/ is awarded to the Petitioner under this head.

Therefore,
the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/ under this head.

17. The Petitioner is entitled compensation under the following heads:
1. Pain & suffering Rs.55,000/
2.

Medical expenses Rs.1,33,558/
3. Loss of income during laid Rs.22,000/ up period 4. Loss of future income Rs.92,400/
5. Loss of future amenities and Rs.17,000/ happiness

6. Attendant, conveyance, food and Rs.17,000/ nourishment charges 7. Future medical expenses Rs. 20,000/ TOTAL Rs.3,56,958/ The total compensation comes to Rs.3,56,958/ and if it is rounded off it comes to Rs.3,57,000/ and same is awarded to the petitioner.

Liability:
18.

The respondent No.2 contended that as on the date of accident the rider of insured vehicle was not holding valid and effective DL to drive the said category of vehicle which is in contravention of policy conditions and hence they are not liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

In support of said defence the respondent no.2 has examined the RW.1 who has produced the authorization letter,
copy of policy, true copy of chargesheet and unserved RPAD cover with letter sent to insured.

There is no cross examination to the RW.1 but however the petitioner is not competent to prove either the existence of valid DL or not as it is the duty of insured to prove the same but in this case the insured/R1 remained absent and hence the defence of the respondent no.2/Insurance Company is proved.

Moreover, the Ex.R.3 clearly shows that IO after conducting complete investigation has also put relevant Section against accused for not holding valid and effective DL as on the date of accident, this document also clearly supports the defence of the respondent No.2.

By leading the evidence of RW.1 and relying on the Ex.P.3/Ex.R3 the respondent No.2 has successfully proved their defence that the rider of the offending insured vehicle had no valid and effective DL as on the date of accident and hence there is breach of policy conditions.
Sri.Ramappa vs Mr.Narendra on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187077521/
7 19.

The respondent No.2 further contends that as there is a breach of policy conditions and hence they are not liable to pay compensation and pay and recovery principles are also not applicable to the case on hand.

On the other side the counsel for the petitioner submits that as the petitioner is third party and as the third party risk is covered under Ex.R.2 policy and hence if this Tribunal comes to conclusion that there is a breach of policy conditions then the pay and recovery needs to be ordered.

The counsel for the respondent No.2 relied upon the decisions which are referred above with regard to principle of pay and recovery, they are not applicable to the present case as the facts and circumstance are different and in view of the decision of Hon'ble H.C. in MFA.No:30131/2010 (MVI) in the case of New India Assurance Co. Ltd., vs. Yallavva and Anr., wherein also principles of pay and recovery observed.

entities.text: New India Assurance Co. Ltd., vs. Yallavva and Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, for the above discussion the respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle is solely liable to pay said compensation to the petitioner.

However, under the principles of pay and recovery as per the above discussion as the policy existed and covered risk of third party, the respondent No.2 being the insurer is directed to pay compensation to the petitioner at the first instance and later to recover the same from the insured owner by filing Execution petition as per law.

Though the Petitioner claimed compensation of Rs.10,00,000, but the Petitioner are entitled only for a sum of Rs.3,57,000/ alongwith interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till date of deposit.
Therefore, the petition needs to be allowed in part.
Accordingly I answer Issue No.3 is partly in the affirmative.
20. Issue No.3:
In view of findings from the above discussions, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER The petition is allowed in part with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,57,000/ (Rupees Three Lakhs Fifty Seven Thousand Only) along with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of depositing the amount.
The Respondent No.1/owner is solely liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
However, the respondent No.2/Insurance Company is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest before this Tribunal within 60 days from the date of this Judgement at the first instance and later to recover it from the respondent No.1/owner by filing execution petition.
On deposit of compensation and interest, entire compensation amount shall be released in favour of the Petitioner as he is senior citizen by way of epayment and on proper identification and due acknowledgment as per Rules.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw decree accordingly.
(Typed to my dictation directly on the computer by the Stenographer, corrected and then pronounced by me in open court on this the 19th day of April 2023).

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with the documents produced as per Exs.P.1 to P.4, P7 to P13, this court is of the opinion that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the TVS Apachi Bike bearing Engine No.BRICH2004673 (Engine & Chassis No.H2004673C04187) and same has resulted in grievous injuries to the Petitioner.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation from the Respondents.
The accident took place in the year 2017.
The respondent No.2 contended that as on the date of accident the rider of insured vehicle was not holding valid and effective DL to drive the said category of vehicle which is in contravention of policy conditions and hence they are not liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
There is no cross examination to the RW.1 but however the petitioner is not competent to prove either the existence of valid DL or not as it is the duty of insured to prove the same but in this case the insured/R1 remained absent and hence the defence of the respondent no.2/Insurance Company is proved.
By leading the evidence of RW.1 and relying on the Ex.P.3/Ex.R3 the respondent No.2 has successfully proved their defence that the rider of the offending insured vehicle had no valid and effective DL as on the date of accident and hence there is breach of policy conditions.
Sri.Ramappa vs Mr.Narendra on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187077521/
7 19.
However, under the principles of pay and recovery as per the above discussion as the policy existed and covered risk of third party, the respondent No.2 being the insurer is directed to pay compensation to the petitioner at the first instance and later to recover the same from the insured owner by filing Execution petition as per law.
